wind.atLanding: Weather at the time of landing
wind.simTitle: Wind at the aircraft according to the simulator (AMBIENT WIND), median {top} → {bottom}

hero.rateSubMeasured: No value from the sim – measured

facts.derivedTitle: The runway was derived from your ground track: its axis is your own line, so the offset from the real centreline cannot be determined from it.
facts.derivedLabel: Centreline · runway derived from your ground track
facts.centrelineWarn: More than a quarter of the runway width off the centreline
facts.rolloutWarn: Rollout ended beyond the runway end
facts.indexTitle: Summary of the raw values – formula under “Methodology”
facts.indexNa: {reason} · only measurable with all parts, see “Methodology”

noRunway.text: No runway matched: within {radius} of the touchdown point there is no runway whose direction matches the heading within ±{heading}. Touchdown point, centreline offset and glide path are not available.

stabilised.noteApproach: Speed against the {vapp} reference ({source}); glide path against the {path}.
stabilised.noteGates: Speed against the {speed} reference ({source}); glide path ±{tol} = {oneDot}, more than {full} ({twoDots}, full scale) is level S2.

landingRate.title: Landing rate:
landingRate.text: the simulator's value (PLANE TOUCHDOWN NORMAL VELOCITY, ×60 in fpm, negative = descending). If the sim delivers no new value (below 1 fpm or unchanged), the vertical speed of the last airborne sample is used. With bounces the hardest contact of this landing event counts, never a peak over the whole flight; two ground contacts with less than {gap} of air between them count as one contact. The flight's landing rate in the logbook is the last full-stop landing.

measured.title: Measured value:
measured.text: the last sample before ground contact from the telemetry stream (at the simulator's frame rate). Because V/S on the ground is meaningless and even a high sample rate can miss the moment of contact, it differs from the sim value. “On the ground” only counts when the height above ground is at most {agl}; the landing is only confirmed after three consecutive ground samples (≥ {confirm}).

gLoad.title: g-load:
gLoad.text: the highest load factor in the half second after each contact (the nose wheel touching down afterwards is not included); implausible values (above {max}, negative) are discarded.

track.title: Track:
track.text: approach, flare and rollout come from the stored track at 1 sample per second. Heights are “above the touchdown point”: altitude MSL minus the MSL of the first ground sample – independent of the terrain under the approach and of the airport elevation in the database. The approach starts at the last descent through {start}, otherwise {fallback} before touchdown.

runway.title: Runway:
runway.source: OurAirports (public domain); coordinates of both runway ends, width from the database (if missing: “width unknown”).
runway.displaced: A displaced threshold from the database moves the threshold along the axis.
runway.displacedHere: A displaced threshold from the database moves the threshold along the axis (here {dist}).
runway.match: The nearest runway within {radius} whose direction matches the heading at touchdown within ±{heading} is matched.
runway.tdz: (ICAO/FAA): from the threshold to {end}, on runways shorter than {short} the first third.
runway.aiming: The aiming point (marking per ICAO Annex 14: {marks} depending on runway length) lies within the zone and is only a mark.
runway.aimingHere: The aiming point (marking per ICAO Annex 14: {marks} depending on runway length, here {here}) lies within the zone and is only a mark.
runway.derived: VectaSim derives the runway from your ground track: axis = the line of your rollout, threshold assumed {offset} before the touchdown point (or at the aiming point of the database length), ±{along} along. The lateral offset is then not measurable; without a known length the touchdown zone is the fixed assumption 0–{tdzEnd} and the rest of the runway is not available. Every further landing there refines the remembered runway.
runway.correct: With “Correct runway …” you set the threshold and end yourself – your runway takes precedence over OurAirports.

glidepath.title: Glide path:
glidepath.text: angle from the touchdown point of the {deg} reference ({tch} above the threshold) to the aircraft, only from {from} before it. Tolerance ±{tol} = {oneDot} (FSF: “within one dot”); ±{full} is full scale ({twoDots}) and is only named as level S2. Without a matched runway it is not available.

stabilised.title: Stabilised approach
stabilised.text: at {gate1} and {gate2} (interpolated): gear down, flaps set, |V/S| ≤ {vs}, IAS {below}/{above} to the reference speed, glide path ±{oneDot}, bank ≤ {bank}. Reference: 1. the Vapp entered for the aircraft (Logbook → Aircraft); 2. otherwise the median of the flown IAS between {from} and {to} – this measures consistency, not whether the speed was right for the type; 3. otherwise {factor} × VS0. This landing: {speed} ({source}).

flare.title: Flare:
flare.text: from the sample after which the sink rate stayed below {pct} of the mean approach sink rate (500–200 ft) until touchdown; resolution 1 s.

wind.title: Wind:
wind.text: the airport's METAR at the time of landing (stored at landing), otherwise the current one – without its own METAR that of the nearest station within {radius} (aviationweather.gov or VATSIM), only for landings in the last {hours}. If the report's observation time is more than {maxAge} before or after touchdown, this is noted with the wind. Headwind/crosswind refer to the runway direction (true); with VRB or a direction range (dddVddd) VectaSim also shows the most unfavourable crosswind within it.

index.title: VectaSim index
index.text: (small, below the raw values, never meant as a verdict):

references.title: Approach references:
references.text: the glide path is an assumed {deg} path over a {tch} threshold crossing height – without procedure data, the real ILS/RNAV angle may differ (“{deg} assumption”). 1 dot of glide path = {gsDot}. Course (localiser substitute): angle from an imaginary antenna {antenna} beyond the runway end, 1 dot = {locDot} at the threshold. “Established” from the first point after which the track stayed within {track} of the runway and the lateral offset within max. {minM} or {ratio} of the distance.

ils.title: ILS from the simulator (from track v2):
ils.text: if NAV 1 receives a valid glide path for at least {share} of the samples {top} → {floor}, it replaces the assumption: angle from NAV RAW GLIDE SLOPE, deviation from NAV GLIDE SLOPE ERROR (“{deg} (ILS)”). Likewise the localiser (NAV CDI, ±127 = ±{fullScale}) replaces the geometry. Both values are always calculated (measurement log); if their medians differ by more than {mismatch}, a note is shown; at more than {rejectGs} of glide path or {rejectLoc} of course the ILS does not belong to this runway and VectaSim assesses geometrically.

vapp.title: Reference speed (Vapp):
vapp.text: 1. the Vapp entered for the aircraft (Logbook → Aircraft); 2. otherwise the median of your own IAS between {from} and {to} on this approach – this assesses the consistency of the speed, not whether it was right for the type; 3. without measurable IAS {factor} × the simulator's VS0 (assumption); 4. otherwise the speed and energy criteria are not available. The SimBrief OFP contains no approach speed. Once VS0 is known, the reference is checked against {min}–{max} × VS0. This approach: {speed} ({source}).

config.title: Configuration and thrust (from track v2, FSF BN 7.1):
config.text: at 1,000 and 500 ft the landing flaps – the setting entered for the aircraft, otherwise the simulator's highest lever position, otherwise the setting at touchdown; N1 at least {n1} below {gate} (idle only counts after {idle}, below {floor} not at all – flare), spoilers extended at most {spoilers}. Without values (older flights, piston engine without N1) the criteria are not available. Autopilot and A/THR appear in the measurement log for information only.

windEnergy.title: Wind and energy:
windEnergy.text: sim wind at the aircraft {top} → {bottom} as the median relative to the runway; notes for tailwind above {tail}, crosswind above {cross} and a change of more than {shear} between {topFt} and the threshold (VectaSim convention). Energy uses the simulator's TAS, otherwise IAS (ISA); band 10 nm → 1,000 ft on final: too high from {high}, too low from {low}.

gates.title: Gates:
gates.text: 10 nm – altitude ±{tenAlt} to the path and energy ≤ {tenEnergy} (only when established), IAS ≤ {tenIas}; FAF ({fafDist} before the threshold or {fafHat}, whichever comes first) – gear, flaps ≥ 1, altitude ±{fafAlt}, speed {fafBelow}/{fafAbove}; 1,000 and 500 ft – gear ≥ {gear}, landing flaps, |V/S| ≤ {vs}, speed {below}/{above}, glide path and course ±{dots}, bank ≤ {bank}; 50 ft values only. Values are interpolated at the last crossing. “Not measurable” never counts as “not met”.

stability.title: Stability and 3-second rule:
stability.text: the window {top} → {bottom} is assessed (glide path down to {gsFloor}). A deviation only counts once it lasts its minimum duration without interruption – speed {speedS}, bank {bankS}, sink rate {vsS1} (S2 {vsS2}), glide path and course {gsS}; shorter excursions under {momentary} count as momentary values. Level S1/S2: speed {speed1} or {speed2}, sink rate {vs}, glide path {gs}, course {loc}, bank {bank}. “Stable from” is the highest height (up to {stableMax}, rounded down to {round}) from which nothing was exceeded down to {bottom}.

bands.title: Bands:
bands.text: {stable} – no exceedance; {deviations} – 1–2 criteria above 500 ft, none below; {unstable} – 3 or more criteria above 500 ft; {unstableBelow500} – at least one exceedance below 500 ft (per EASA / Data4Safety). A go-around is not a band but the outcome of the approach.

resolution.title: Resolution:
resolution.text: based on the stored track at 1 sample per second (thinned to one every {sparse} above {dense}). Durations are whole seconds; the analysis does not see peaks between two samples. Heights are above the touchdown point (HAT); for a go-around above the airport elevation from the database.
